chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from one of his companions, from Abu Ja'far or Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The sun does not rise on a day superior to the day of Friday, and the speech of the birds in it, when some meet others, is: 'Peace, peace! A good day.'
ai.seo_question: What makes the day of Friday superior in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi underscores the cosmic significance of Friday, a day revered in Shia tradition as the feast of Allah and the day of the Prophet's birth, where creation itself proclaims its sanctity. The mention of birds saying 'Salam' reflects the broader theological concept of the day's inherent peace and the special attention bestowed upon the Ahl al-Bayt, aligning with the Friday prayer's role as a weekly renewal of allegiance.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Ibrahim Bin Abu Al Balaat, from one of his companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> or Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Never does the sun emerge on a day superior than the day of Friday, and the speech of the bird during it when they meet each other is, ‘Peace! Peace! (It is) a devotional day’.
en.sarwar: 11. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Ibrahim ibn abu al-Balad from certain individuals of his people who have said the following: “Abu Ja’far or abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
There is no other day on which sun shines more excellent than Friday. The words of birds, on meeting each other, on this day are, “Peace, peace. It is a good day.’””
